newsitem.title: USA: American Air pilots call talks "slow and difficult".
newsitem.headline: American Air pilots call talks "slow and difficult".

text.p: The head of the American Airlines pilots' union said Friday contract talks were difficult and that no common ground has been reached in the negotiations aimed at averting a strike after midnight.

James Sovich, president of the Allied Pilots Association, urged the carrier to "do the right thing" and reach an agreement. Asked about the pace of the talks, he told reporters that they were "slow and difficult." The negotiations, which opened Monday morning and are being guided by a federal mediator, are aimed at an agreement before the deadline of just after midnight set by the pilots.
Sovich said the issues of pay and of who will fly the new small jets American plans to buy for its regional carrier, American Eagle, were equally important.
He said the 11 percent wage increase sought by the union would not keep pace with inflation, since the raises would run through 2000 and the union has not had an increase since 1993.
Asked if there was any common ground reached on the regional jet issue, he said, "Not to date."
American wants to use lower-paid pilots for its new jets, a move the union opposes, in order to compete with other major carriers who operate low-cost commuter services.
